subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Definition of a Business (Optional Concentration Test)
question: Titan Holdings Ltd. acquires 100% equity in an unlisted entity whose sole asset is an operating commercial office tower leased to corporate tenants. The gross asset value is ₹100 Crores, of which the office building represents ₹98 Crores (including fair value of leases), and other assets (cash and receivables) represent ₹2 Crores. Management elects to apply the optional concentration test under Ind AS 103. What is the conclusion?
options: The acquisition is automatically classified as a business combination requiring goodwill calculation.

The concentration test is met because substantially all (98%) of the fair value of the gross assets acquired is concentrated in a single identifiable asset (the building); therefore, the set of activities and assets is NOT a business, and the transaction is accounted for as an Asset Acquisition (no goodwill recognized).
The concentration test fails and mandatory purchase price allocation must be performed.
All real estate acquisitions are treated as joint ventures.
ref: Ind AS 103 (Business Combinations) - Appendix B Paragraphs B7A-B7C: Optional Concentration Test
explanation: Under the revised Ind AS 103, an entity may elect to apply an optional concentration test to assess whether an acquired set of activities and assets is not a business. The concentration test is met if substantially all of the fair value of the gross assets acquired is concentrated in a single identifiable asset (or a group of similar identifiable assets). When met, the acquisition is an asset acquisition, and goodwill is not recognized.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Contingent Consideration Classification & Remeasurement
question: On 1st April 2023, Acquirer Ltd. acquires 100% of Target Ltd. The purchase agreement requires Acquirer Ltd. to pay an additional ₹10 Crores cash to the former owners if Target Ltd.'s revenue exceeds ₹100 Crores in Year 2. At acquisition date, the fair value of this contingent consideration is ₹6 Crores. On 31st March 2024, revised forecasts indicate revenue will surge, increasing the fair value of the contingent obligation to ₹8.5 Crores. How should the contingent consideration and its subsequent change be accounted for under Ind AS 103?
options: Classified as Equity; subsequent fair value change of ₹2.5 Crores is recognized in OCI.

Classified as a Financial Liability (an obligation to deliver cash); at acquisition date, ₹6 Crores is included in consideration transferred (increasing Goodwill); subsequent increase of ₹2.5 Crores is recognized as a fair value loss in the Statement of Profit and Loss (not adjusted against Goodwill).
Goodwill is adjusted retrospectively by ₹2.5 Crores on 31st March 2024.
Omitted until Year 2 when cash is paid.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs 39-40 & 58: Contingent Consideration Classification and Subsequent Measurement
explanation: Contingent consideration that gives rise to an obligation to deliver cash is classified as a financial liability under Ind AS 32 and measured at fair value at acquisition date (included in purchase consideration). Under Ind AS 103 Paragraph 58, subsequent changes in fair value that are not measurement period adjustments are recognized in profit or loss, and cannot adjust Goodwill.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: NCI Measurement - Fair Value vs Proportionate Share
question: Parent Ltd. acquires 80% of Subsidiary Ltd. for ₹80 Crores cash. The fair value of Subsidiary Ltd.'s identifiable net assets is ₹70 Crores. The fair value of the 20% Non-Controlling Interest (NCI) is ₹18 Crores. Compare the Goodwill recognized under Method 1 (NCI at Fair Value - Full Goodwill) and Method 2 (NCI at Proportionate Share of Net Identifiable Assets - Partial Goodwill) under Ind AS 103:
options: Method 1 Goodwill = ₹28 Crores; Method 2 Goodwill = ₹24 Crores.

Method 1 (Full Goodwill): Consideration (₹80 Cr) + NCI at Fair Value (₹18 Cr) - Net Assets (₹70 Cr) = ₹28 Crores; Method 2 (Partial Goodwill): Consideration (₹80 Cr) + NCI at 20% of Net Assets (₹14 Cr) - Net Assets (₹70 Cr) = ₹24 Crores.
Both methods yield identical goodwill of ₹10 Crores.
Goodwill under Method 2 is negative (bargain purchase).
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraph 19 & Paragraph 32: Measurement of Non-Controlling Interest
explanation: Ind AS 103 Paragraph 19 allows the acquirer to measure NCI at the acquisition date either at fair value (Method 1: Full Goodwill = ₹80 + ₹18 - ₹70 = ₹28 Cr) or at the NCI's proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets (Method 2: Partial Goodwill = ₹80 + 20% of ₹70 - ₹70 = ₹80 + ₹14 - ₹70 = ₹24 Cr).

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Bargain Purchase Gain (Capital Reserve)
question: On 1st April 2023, Acquirer Ltd. acquires 100% of Target Ltd. for ₹40 Crores cash in a distressed sale. The fair value of identifiable net assets acquired is ₹50 Crores. Acquirer Ltd. conducts a thorough reassessment under Ind AS 103 Paragraph 36 and confirms all assets and liabilities were correctly identified and measured. How should the resulting ₹10 Crores excess be recognized under Ind AS 103?
options: Recognized immediately in Profit or Loss as an exceptional operating profit.

Recognized in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) on acquisition date and accumulated in Equity as Capital Reserve; however, if there is no clear evidence of the underlying reason for the bargain purchase, it is recognized directly in equity as Capital Reserve without routing through OCI.
Credited to General Reserve.
Deferred as a liability in the balance sheet.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs 34-36A: Bargain Purchase Gain & Capital Reserve
explanation: Under Ind AS 103 (which differs from IFRS 3), a bargain purchase gain is recognized in Other Comprehensive Income and accumulated in equity as capital reserve, provided there is clear evidence of the underlying reason for the bargain purchase (such as a distressed sale). If there is no clear evidence, it is recognized directly in equity as Capital Reserve.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Acquisition-Related Costs Treatment
question: In executing the acquisition of Target Ltd., Acquirer Ltd. incurred: (i) ₹3 Crores in fees paid to investment bankers, legal advisors, and accountants for due diligence; and (ii) ₹2 Crores in stamp duty and registration fees for issuing new equity shares as purchase consideration. How should these costs be accounted for under Ind AS 103?
options: All ₹5 Crores capitalized as part of Goodwill.

Advisory, due diligence, and legal fees of ₹3 Crores are recognized as an expense in Profit or Loss in the period incurred; share issue costs of ₹2 Crores are deducted directly from equity (Securities Premium) under Ind AS 32.
All ₹5 Crores deducted from Securities Premium.
All ₹5 Crores expensed in P&L.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraph 53: Acquisition-Related Costs
explanation: Ind AS 103 Paragraph 53 states that acquisition-related costs (finder's fees, advisory, legal, accounting, valuation and other professional fees) are expensed in the periods in which the costs are incurred and the services are received. Costs to issue debt or equity securities are recognized in accordance with Ind AS 32 and Ind AS 109 (deducted from equity proceeds).

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Definition of Control - Three Core Elements
question: Which of the following sets of elements must ALL be present simultaneously for an investor to control an investee under Ind AS 110?
options: Ownership of more than 50% equity shares, board majority, and debt ownership.

(a) Power over the investee; (b) exposure, or rights, to variable returns from its involvement with the investee; and (c) the ability to use its power over the investee to affect the amount of the investor's returns.
Power of attorney, joint venture agreement, and equity participation.
Holding at least 20% voting rights with significant influence.
ref: Ind AS 110 (Consolidated Financial Statements) - Paragraph 7: Definition of Control
explanation: Under Ind AS 110 Paragraph 7, an investor controls an investee if and only if the investor has all the following: (a) power over the investee (existing rights that give it the current ability to direct relevant activities); (b) exposure, or rights, to variable returns from its involvement with the investee; and (c) the ability to use its power over the investee to affect the amount of the investor's returns.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: De Facto Control (Substantive vs Potential Rights)
question: PQR Ltd. holds 42% of the voting rights in XYZ Ltd. The remaining 58% is widely dispersed among 25,000 retail shareholders, none of whom holds more than 0.1%. At the last three Annual General Meetings, only 60% of total voting rights were cast in person or by proxy, and PQR Ltd.'s 42% represented 70% of the votes cast, allowing it to unilaterally appoint the entire Board of Directors. Does PQR Ltd. control XYZ Ltd. under Ind AS 110?
options: No, control requires a minimum statutory threshold of 50.01% equity voting rights.

Yes, PQR Ltd. has 'de facto control' because its voting rights are sufficient to give it power over the investee when evaluated in conjunction with the size of its holding relative to the dispersion of other holdings and historical shareholder attendance patterns at general meetings.
PQR Ltd. has significant influence only and must use the equity method under Ind AS 28.
XYZ Ltd. must be accounted for as an associate.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraphs B41-B45: De Facto Control and Voting Rights Dispersion
explanation: Ind AS 110 clarifies that an investor can have power even if it holds less than a majority of the voting rights (de facto control). An investor considers all facts and circumstances, including the size of its holding relative to the dispersion of other vote holders, attendance patterns, and potential voting rights. The widely dispersed retail base enables PQR Ltd. to direct relevant activities unilaterally.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Elimination of Intra-Group Unrealized Profit on Inventory
question: Parent Ltd. owns 75% of Subsidiary Ltd. During FY 2023-24, Subsidiary Ltd. sells inventory to Parent Ltd. for ₹40 Crores at a profit margin of 25% on selling price (profit ₹10 Crores). At year-end, 50% of this inventory remains unsold in Parent Ltd.'s warehouse. How is the unrealized intra-group profit eliminated in the consolidated financial statements?
options: Eliminate ₹10 Crores fully from Parent Ltd.'s retained earnings.

Eliminate unrealized profit of ₹5 Crores (50% of ₹10 Cr) by reducing consolidated inventory by ₹5 Crores; because this is an 'upstream' sale by the subsidiary, the ₹5 Crores profit elimination is allocated between Parent's share (75% = ₹3.75 Cr) and Non-Controlling Interest (25% = ₹1.25 Cr).
No elimination is needed if the transfer was executed at fair market value.
Eliminate ₹5 Crores against Goodwill.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraph B86(c): Elimination of Intra-Group Profits & Upstream Allocation
explanation: Ind AS 110 Paragraph B86(c) requires elimination in full of intra-group assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses and cash flows relating to transactions between entities of the group. For an upstream sale (subsidiary to parent), unrealized profit in ending inventory (₹5 Cr) is eliminated against the subsidiary's profit, thereby reducing both the parent's share of consolidated profit and the Non-Controlling Interest pro rata.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Changes in Ownership Interest Without Loss of Control
question: Parent Ltd. owns 80% of Subsidiary Ltd. (carrying amount of NCI is ₹30 Crores). Parent Ltd. acquires an additional 10% equity stake from non-controlling shareholders for ₹18 Crores cash, increasing its holding to 90%. How should this transaction be recorded in the consolidated financial statements under Ind AS 110?
options: Calculate additional Goodwill of ₹3 Crores in the consolidated balance sheet.

Accounted for as an equity transaction: NCI is reduced by its proportionate carrying amount of ₹15 Crores (10%/20% of ₹30 Cr), and the difference of ₹3 Crores between consideration paid (₹18 Cr) and the adjustment to NCI (₹15 Cr) is recognized directly in Equity (Retained Earnings) attributable to the parent; NO goodwill or P&L gain/loss is recognized.
Recognize an impairment loss of ₹3 Crores in Profit or Loss.
Recognize ₹3 Crores in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraphs 23 & B96: Changes in Proportion Held by Non-Controlling Interests
explanation: Ind AS 110 Paragraph 23 states that changes in a parent's ownership interest in a subsidiary that do not result in a loss of control are accounted for as equity transactions (transactions with owners in their capacity as owners). Any difference between the amount by which NCI is adjusted and the fair value of consideration paid or received is recognized directly in equity.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Loss of Control and Retained Investment Fair Valuation
question: Parent Ltd. owns 100% of Subsidiary Ltd. with net assets of ₹80 Crores and goodwill of ₹20 Crores (total carrying amount ₹100 Crores). Parent Ltd. sells a 70% stake for ₹105 Crores cash, losing control. The fair value of the retained 30% investment is ₹45 Crores. Parent Ltd. will account for the retained 30% as an associate under Ind AS 28. What is the total gain on loss of control recognized in Profit or Loss under Ind AS 110?
options: ₹5 Crores (₹105 Crores sale proceeds minus ₹100 Crores carrying amount).

₹50 Crores (Aggregate of consideration received ₹105 Cr + fair value of retained 30% investment ₹45 Cr = ₹150 Cr, minus derecognition of net assets and goodwill ₹100 Cr = ₹50 Crores gain recognized in Profit or Loss).
₹35 Crores recognized in OCI.
Zero gain; proceeds are credited to capital reserve.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraph 25 & Paragraph B98: Gain or Loss on Loss of Control
explanation: Under Ind AS 110 Paragraph B98, if a parent loses control of a subsidiary, it shall: (a) derecognize the assets (including goodwill) and liabilities of the subsidiary; (b) recognize the fair value of consideration received; (c) recognize any retained investment at its fair value at the date control is lost; and (d) recognize the resulting difference as a gain or loss in profit or loss attributable to the parent.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Measurement Period Adjustments
question: Acquirer Ltd. acquired Target Ltd. on 1st November 2023. At acquisition date, an environmental cleanup liability was provisionally measured at ₹5 Crores. On 15th July 2024 (within the 12-month measurement period), new expert hydrological reports obtained based on facts and circumstances that existed at the acquisition date reveal that the actual cleanup liability was ₹9 Crores. How should this ₹4 Crores increase be accounted for under Ind AS 103?
options: Recognize an expense of ₹4 Crores in Profit or Loss for FY 2024-25.

Retrospectively adjust the provisional accounting: increase the environmental liability by ₹4 Crores and increase Goodwill by ₹4 Crores as a measurement period adjustment, as if the accounting had been completed at the acquisition date.
Recognize ₹4 Crores in Other Comprehensive Income.
Measurement period adjustments are prohibited after 6 months.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs 45-50: Measurement Period Adjustments
explanation: Under Ind AS 103 Paragraph 45, if the initial accounting for a business combination is incomplete by the end of the reporting period, the acquirer reports provisional amounts. During the measurement period (not exceeding one year from acquisition date), the acquirer shall retrospectively adjust provisional amounts recognized at the acquisition date to reflect new information obtained about facts and circumstances that existed as of the acquisition date, adjusting Goodwill accordingly.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Step Acquisition (Business Combination Achieved in Stages)
question: Alpha Ltd. held a 20% equity investment in Beta Ltd. carried at fair value of ₹25 Crores (cost was ₹20 Crores, with cumulative fair value gain of ₹5 Crores recognized in OCI). On 1st April 2023, Alpha Ltd. acquires an additional 60% stake in Beta Ltd. for ₹90 Crores cash, gaining control. At acquisition date, the fair value of Alpha Ltd.'s initial 20% stake is ₹30 Crores. How is the initial 20% stake treated under Ind AS 103?
options: Carried forward at historical cost of ₹20 Crores.

Remeasured to its acquisition-date fair value of ₹30 Crores; the resulting gain of ₹10 Crores (or reclassification of prior OCI amounts) is recognized in Profit or Loss, and total consideration transferred for the 80% stake is ₹120 Crores (₹90 Cr cash + ₹30 Cr fair value of previous holding).
Credited directly to Securities Premium.
No remeasurement is permitted.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs 41-42: Business Combination Achieved in Stages
explanation: In a business combination achieved in stages, the acquirer shall remeasure its previously held equity interest in the acquiree at its acquisition-date fair value and recognize the resulting gain or loss in profit or loss. Any amounts previously recognized in other comprehensive income in respect of that interest are accounted for on the same basis as would be required if the acquirer had disposed directly of the previously held interest.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Investment Entity Exemption from Consolidation
question: Ventures Fund Ltd. meets all criteria of an 'Investment Entity' under Ind AS 110 (it obtains funds from investors, its business purpose is investing solely for capital appreciation and investment income, and it measures all investments at fair value). Ventures Fund Ltd. owns 80% of an operating tech startup. How should Ventures Fund Ltd. account for this subsidiary in its financial statements?
options: It must prepare consolidated financial statements and consolidate the subsidiary line-by-line.
It is exempt from consolidating the subsidiary; instead, it must measure the investment in the subsidiary at Fair Value Through Profit or Loss (FVTPL) in accordance with Ind AS 109.
Account for it using the equity method under Ind AS 28.
Account for it at historical cost under Ind AS 27.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraphs 31-33: Investment Entity Exemption
explanation: Ind AS 110 Paragraph 31 provides an explicit exception to consolidation: an investment entity shall not consolidate its subsidiaries or apply Ind AS 103 when it obtains control of another entity. Instead, an investment entity shall measure an investment in a subsidiary at fair value through profit or loss in accordance with Ind AS 109 (except for subsidiaries that provide investment-related services to the investment entity).

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Uniform Accounting Policies in Consolidation
question: Parent Ltd. measures its manufacturing plant using the Cost Model under Ind AS 16. Its subsidiary, Sub Ltd., measures its manufacturing plant using the Revaluation Model under Ind AS 16. When preparing the Consolidated Financial Statements of the group under Ind AS 110, how must this difference be handled?
options: Parent Ltd. can simply aggregate the figures without any adjustments because each company is an independent legal entity.

Consolidated financial statements must be prepared using uniform accounting policies for like transactions and other events in similar circumstances; Sub Ltd.'s plant must be adjusted to the Cost Model in the consolidation worksheets to conform with the parent's group accounting policy.
Parent Ltd. must switch to the Revaluation Model across all group companies.
The subsidiary must be excluded from consolidation.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraph B87: Uniform Accounting Policies
explanation: Ind AS 110 Paragraph B87 specifies: 'If a member of the group uses accounting policies other than those adopted in the consolidated financial statements for like transactions and events in similar circumstances, appropriate adjustments are made to that group member's financial statements in preparing the consolidated financial statements to ensure conformity with the group's accounting policies.'

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Pre-Existing Relationships Settlement
question: Prior to acquisition, Acquirer Ltd. and Target Ltd. were in litigation where Acquirer Ltd. was suing Target Ltd. for breach of supply contract. On 1st April 2023, Acquirer Ltd. acquires 100% of Target Ltd. for ₹100 Crores. At acquisition date, the fair value of the pending lawsuit was ₹10 Crores. How is this pre-existing relationship accounted for under Ind AS 103?
options: Included entirely in the purchase consideration for Target Ltd.

Treated as a separate transaction from the business combination; Acquirer Ltd. recognizes a settlement of the pre-existing legal relationship (debiting/crediting P&L for any gain/loss on settlement) and allocates only the remaining consideration of ₹90 Crores to the business combination.
Ignored and written off to General Reserve.
Recognized as an impairment of goodwill.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs 51-52 & Paragraphs B51-B53: Settlement of Pre-Existing Relationships
explanation: Ind AS 103 requires an acquirer to determine whether a transaction is part of the business combination or a separate transaction. A pre-existing relationship (such as a contract or lawsuit) between the acquirer and acquiree that is settled in connection with the combination is accounted for separately. Any settlement gain or loss is recognized in profit or loss and excluded from consideration transferred.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Elimination of Intra-Group Fixed Asset Transfer
question: On 1st April 2023, Parent Ltd. sells an item of plant to its 80% subsidiary for ₹50 Lakhs (carrying amount in Parent's books was ₹30 Lakhs; profit ₹20 Lakhs). Subsidiary Ltd. depreciates the plant over its remaining useful life of 5 years on a straight-line basis (depreciation ₹10 Lakhs/year). On 31st March 2024, how is this intra-group plant transfer adjusted in the consolidated financial statements?
options: Eliminate ₹20 Lakhs profit against Plant; eliminate ₹4 Lakhs excess depreciation (₹20L / 5 years) by crediting depreciation expense; net reduction in consolidated plant carrying amount is ₹16 Lakhs, with net reduction in consolidated profit of ₹16 Lakhs.
Eliminate full ₹20 Lakhs permanently without depreciation adjustments.
No adjustment is made because the subsidiary paid market price.
Eliminate ₹20 Lakhs against NCI.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraph B86: Elimination of Intra-Group Profits on Depreciable Assets
explanation: In consolidated financial statements, the plant must appear as if the transfer never occurred: carrying amount = ₹30L - (1/5 × ₹30L) = ₹24 Lakhs. Subsidiary's book value = ₹50L - ₹10L = ₹40 Lakhs. Elimination entry reduces Plant by ₹16 Lakhs (₹40L - ₹24L), reduces Parent profit by ₹20L, and reduces depreciation expense by ₹4 Lakhs (net impact on consolidated profit = -₹16 Lakhs).

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Indemnification Assets
question: In a business combination, the seller provides a contractual indemnity to Acquirer Ltd. to reimburse up to ₹15 Crores for any unfavorable outcome arising from a pre-acquisition tax litigation of Target Ltd. At acquisition date, Acquirer recognizes a tax litigation provision of ₹10 Crores under Ind AS 37. How should Acquirer Ltd. recognize the indemnification asset under Ind AS 103?
options: At maximum indemnity cap of ₹15 Crores.

At the same time and on the same measurement basis as the indemnified item: an indemnification asset of ₹10 Crores is recognized on acquisition date, subject to any contractual limitations or collectibility assessment.
Recognized in OCI as a reserve.
Indemnification assets are not recognized under Ind AS.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs 27-28: Indemnification Assets
explanation: Ind AS 103 Paragraph 27 states that the acquirer shall recognize an indemnification asset at the same time and measured on the same basis as the indemnified item, subject to the need for a valuation allowance for uncollectible amounts. If the indemnified liability is measured at ₹10 Crores, the indemnification asset is recognized at ₹10 Crores.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Potential Voting Rights in Assessing Control
question: Alpha Ltd. holds 40% of the voting shares of Beta Ltd. Gamma Ltd. holds 60%. However, Alpha Ltd. holds currently exercisable call options to acquire an additional 25% voting shares from Gamma Ltd. at a deep discount to market price. How do these potential voting rights impact the assessment of control under Ind AS 110?
options: Potential voting rights are completely ignored until they are legally exercised and registered.

Currently exercisable substantive potential voting rights must be considered; because the call options are currently exercisable and deeply in the money (giving Alpha Ltd. the practical ability to direct relevant activities), Alpha Ltd. has power over Beta Ltd. and controls Beta Ltd.
Control is split 50:50 between Alpha and Gamma.
Potential voting rights require consolidation only if Gamma consents.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraphs B47-B50: Substantive Potential Voting Rights
explanation: Ind AS 110 states that when assessing whether an investor has power, the investor considers its potential voting rights as well as potential voting rights held by other parties. Potential voting rights are considered only if the rights are substantive (i.e. the holder has the practical ability to exercise them, such as when options are currently exercisable and in the money).

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 103: Intangible Assets Not Recognized in Acquiree's Separate Books
question: In acquiring Target Software Ltd., Acquirer Ltd. identifies an unpatented proprietary source code algorithm and an active customer relationship contract portfolio. Neither item was recognized on Target Software Ltd.'s historical balance sheet because they were internally generated. Can Acquirer Ltd. recognize these items as Intangible Assets in the business combination under Ind AS 103?
options: No, only assets that were previously recognized on the acquiree's balance sheet can be recognized.

Yes, the acquirer recognizes separately from goodwill the identifiable intangible assets acquired in a business combination if they meet either the 'separability criterion' or the 'contractual-legal criterion', regardless of whether they were recognized by the acquiree prior to the combination.
They must be subsumed into Goodwill.
Recognized in Other Comprehensive Income.
ref: Ind AS 103 - Paragraphs B31-B34: Identifiable Intangible Assets in Business Combinations
explanation: Ind AS 103 Paragraph B31 states that the acquirer recognizes separately from goodwill the identifiable intangible assets acquired in a business combination. An intangible asset is identifiable if it meets either the contractual-legal criterion (customer contracts) or the separability criterion (unpatented software/code capable of being sold or licensed), even if not recognized by the acquiree prior to acquisition.

subject: Financial Reporting
topicTitle: Business Combinations and Consolidated Financial Statements
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 110: Allocation of Comprehensive Income to NCI
question: Subsidiary Ltd. incurs a total comprehensive loss of ₹40 Crores during the year. Non-Controlling Interest (NCI) holds a 20% stake. Historically, NCI's carrying amount was ₹5 Crores. If the 20% share of current losses (₹8 Crores) is allocated to NCI, its balance will become negative (-₹3 Crores). Under Ind AS 110, can NCI have a deficit (negative) balance?
options: No, NCI can never be negative; any loss exceeding NCI's carrying amount must be absorbed 100% by the parent.

Yes, profit or loss and each component of Other Comprehensive Income shall be attributed to the owners of the parent and to non-controlling interests even if this results in the non-controlling interests having a deficit balance.
The subsidiary must be liquidated immediately.
NCI is reset to zero and the excess is recorded in a suspense account.
ref: Ind AS 110 - Paragraph B94: Attribution of Losses to NCI Resulting in Deficit Balance
explanation: Ind AS 110 Paragraph B94 explicitly states: 'Profit or loss and each component of other comprehensive income are attributed to the owners of the parent and to the non-controlling interests. Total comprehensive income is attributed to the owners of the parent and to the non-controlling interests even if this results in the non-controlling interests having a deficit balance.' NCI can be negative.
